published_prior_art.cite: EmamiPass2024 gives discrete non-Monge examples and Haus2015 studies bottleneck/mixability approximations, but neither gives a same-N scalar signed-quadratic additive O(N^-1) realization theorem with this construction.
EmamiPass2024 and Friesecke2019 establish non-Monge phenomena, not the stated bounded scalar all-N family with an exact 1/(46080N) gap.
Haus2015 is the closest same-row permutation literature, while GaoGeQian2025 optimizes the fractional MOT value; neither states the same-marginal fractional-to-row Theta(N^-1) frontier.
AronowGreenLee2014, Lemma 1 and equations (7)-(11), supplies the sharp two-arm quantile covariance and variance endpoints recovered here.

GaoGeQian2025 gives the fractional causal MOT identified set and BrennanEtAl2025 computes worst-case copulas numerically; neither provides the proposed analytic same-N primal--dual certificate around the realizable endpoint.

AronowGreenLee2014 gives two-arm sharp-bound plug-ins and GaoGeQian2025 gives fractional-MOT plug-in theory, but neither treats the realizable three-arm endpoint with the displayed without-replacement certificate.
The inspected empirical-Monge and mixability papers give examples, structural failures, or bottleneck approximation, not the normalized same-marginal signed-quadratic extremal constant.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract; PMLR bibliographic record and PDF link
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The published paper obtains the exact partial identified set through K-marginal MOT, gives plug-in convergence for the l2 variance cost that is minimax optimal for arbitrary K and d<=4, and extends the convergence result to general quadratic objectives.

source_verification_receipts.version: Operations Research Forum 6, article 46 (version of record, 7 April 2025)
source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract, especially the discrete d=2, three-marginal, three-support-point counterexample and the d=1/m=2 boundary cases
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper supplies a discrete quadratic non-Monge counterexample for three empirical marginals in dimension two, while recording the two-marginal, scalar, and two-point-support cases where Monge solutions exist; it does not state a same-N signed scalar quadratic integrality-gap rate.

source_verification_receipts.version: Author preprint corresponding to Annals of Statistics 42(3), 2014
source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 3, Lemma 1; Appendix proof lines 180-184; Proposition 1 discussion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The two-arm paper derives sharp variance bounds from comonotone and countermonotone quantile couplings and establishes plug-in sharp-bound estimation under complete randomization.

Haus studies column-permutation complete mixability and multidimensional bottleneck assignment, proving hardness and fixed-dimension approximation results for bottleneck row sums rather than an additive average squared-cost fractional-to-integral rate.

The paper proposes an integer program that numerically computes a worst-case copula for causal bootstrap and proves asymptotic validity over several assignment mechanisms and linear/quadratic treatment estimators; it does not provide a universal analytic realization-width theorem.

source_verification_receipts.version: Author preprint corresponding to SIAM Journal on Mathematical Analysis 51(6), 2019
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives a finite three-marginal, three-site non-Monge example through the geometry of symmetric Kantorovich plans, not an all-denominator scalar signed-contrast gap frontier.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add an instance-adaptive certificate theorem whose reported width is controlled by computable support geometry, rather than only the intentionally loose universal constant 3456.

State and analyze at least one nontrivial multi-arm trial-sized worked example, including the fractional optimum, the rounded schedule, and the resulting variance interval, to make the practical gain over an integer program auditable.
Develop a fixed-K extension with explicit dependence on K and contrast geometry; this is the natural path from a field-level three-arm frontier to a broader transport-rounding contribution.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 on the field-tier three-arm same-marginal rounding frontier; retain the two-arm result only as its verified sanity boundary.
